A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DIST2Loss with the same authors, method, and experimental program. The text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting and v2's added checklist.

before.justification: v1 reports original regression, visual grounding, robotic manipulation, reward modeling, and image generation results, including ablations and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices. Their retention from v1 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: The distance-derived categorical targets, KL regularization, contrastive target augmentation, place-value weighting, and embedding-distance extension remain unchanged. Section 2 adds no algorithmic component or architectural modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic linear regression, the RefCOCO family, VIMABench L1/L2, HelpSteer2 with RewardBench and MT-Bench evaluation, and ImageNet generation. Appendix benchmark subdivisions and task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches throughout the corresponding tables and ablations. Ferretv2 remains in Table 1 despite shortened prose, and the newly cited meta-learning works are not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: v2 Section 3.1 reports 5,000 regression training steps at learning rate 1e-5 with batch size 1, substantially differing from v1 Appendix A.2's approximately 250 sample exposures at 2e-5. However, v2 Appendix A.2 retains the original settings. This establishes a substantial change in the reported protocol, with unresolved internal inconsistency; it does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The illustrative comparison of model predictions against individual regression functions is reduced from three examples in v1 Figure 3 to two in v2 Figure 2. The component ablations, VQ token-replacement analysis, and appendix reward and grounding case analyses are otherwise retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-seed regression reporting, ten-seed ablation reporting, and the same mean/std columns. v2's checklist acknowledges insufficient resources for statistical-significance reporting, but introduces no changed run counts, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–9 and the aggregate regression curves match. The limited removal is the third illustrative regression prediction example from v1 Figure 3; v2 Figure 2 retains two. No improved scores or new aggregate findings are reported.

T1.justification: The metric-space definitions and mathematical formulations in Equations 1–9 are retained. Neither version provides formal theorems or proofs, and v2 introduces no new derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: distance-aware training compatible with existing autoregressive architectures, improved convergence and data efficiency across the same applications, and no added inference cost.

C2.justification: v2 expands the rationale for extremely limited regression supervision as a test of structural generalization. It also softens the infinite-resource limitation from 'cannot outperform' cross-entropy to 'may yield no advantage' and newly acknowledges computational constraints on significance reporting.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies regression batch size 1 and adds conflicting training-budget and learning-rate statements in Section 3.1. Its checklist also explicitly promises a documented code release without providing access. The existing hardware tables and other appendix implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Neural Arithmetic Logic Units and Meta-World in Section 3.1 to support its inductive-bias and meta-learning rationale. The broader related-work discussion and positioning of DIST2Loss remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 tightens several introductory and experimental passages, expands the regression explanation, and merges limitations and future directions into the conclusion. It adds a NeurIPS checklist while retaining the main scientific section order and most method and results prose.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one, removes v1's opening overview figure, and rearranges the method, regression, and VQ illustration panels. Tables and appendix figures are extensively resized and relocated, captions are shortened, and the regression illustration drops one example panel.

improvement.justification: v2 offers a clearer rationale for the low-data regression experiment, but introduces incompatible training instructions: Section 3.1 specifies 5,000 steps at 1e-5 while Appendix A.2 retains approximately 250 sample exposures at 2e-5. This makes the unchanged regression evidence harder to reproduce and interpret. That limited reproducibility decline outweighs the modest explanatory gains; the broader method and empirical evidence remain intact.
